# Manual case: Compiler Explorer, and why the published link has no clang pane

All four probes below were run through Compiler Explorer's compile API with
`ce-probe.py` (in this directory), language `hlsl`, on 2026-08-06.  `hlsl_clang_trunk` and
`dxc_trunk` are rolling builds and are not reproducible over time; treat the *class* of
result as the finding, not an exact revision.

    python ce-probe.py <label> <shader> "hlsl_clang_trunk|-T cs_6_0 -E MainCS"

@llvm-beanz's 2024-06-21 comment -- "I've filed an issue to remove these instructions during
DXIL lowering in Clang" -- makes a clang pane the most interesting comparison available on
this issue, so it was pursued rather than assumed.

---

## 1. `case-compute.hlsl` (the compute restating of the repro)

| compiler | exit | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dxc_1_6_2112` | 5 | `warning: DXIL.dll not found.  Resulting DXIL will not be signed...` then `error: Instructions must be of an allowed type.` / `note: at 'unreachable' in block '#4' of function 'MainCS'.` |
| `dxc_trunk` | 5 | same two error lines, no signing warning |
| `hlsl_clang_trunk` | 1 | `fatal error: error in backend: DXIL atomicrmw not implemented for this resource type`, in `DXILResourceAccess` / `replaceAccess` |

Note the CE `dxc_1_6_2112` pane reproduces the reporter's exact 2019 environment for free:
CE runs Linux builds with no `dxil.dll`, so it prints the same signing warning the issue
quotes -- and validation still runs and still fails.  That is the cleanest available
demonstration that the signing warning is incidental to this bug.

The clang line looks like clang diagnosing something, which is exactly the trap SKILL.md
records from #1702.

## 2. Control: `control-clang-rwbuffer.hlsl`

A three-line compute shader with the same `RWBuffer<float4>` store and the same flags,
containing nothing to do with this issue.

```
hlsl_clang_trunk  exit=0    (only "argument unused during compilation: '-Qembed_debug'")
```

Clean.  So clang's failure in probe 1 is **not** a blanket "this backend cannot lower
compute shaders that write an RWBuffer" -- it is about something in the repro.  Under
SKILL.md that is the case where a rejection must not be waved away, so it was narrowed.

## 3. Discriminator: `case-compute-default.hlsl`

Probe 1's shader with the `default:` arm added -- i.e. the input DXC accepts, and the one
the reporter identified as the workaround.

```
hlsl_clang_trunk  exit=1    fatal error: error in backend: DXIL atomicrmw not implemented
                            for this resource type      <-- identical failure
```

A **known-good** input fails clang identically.  The clang failure is therefore unrelated to
#2331; it tracks `ConstantBuffer<T>` plus the buffer store, not the fall-off-the-end path.
A clang pane on this repro would be pure noise, so the published link carries DXC panes
only.

"Known-good" is measured, not assumed -- both this shader and the probe-2 control were also
run locally on ground truth, where they compile clean:

```
variant-compute-default-main-debug.txt          exit=0   no-repro
variant-clang-control-rwbuffer-main-debug.txt   exit=0   no-repro
```

## 4. Supplementary: `case-clang-minimal.hlsl`

Not the repro and not published -- a cut-down restating with the `ConstantBuffer<T>` removed,
which clang's backend can compile, keeping the enum-class switch that covers every
enumerator with no `default:` in a non-void function.

```
dxc_trunk         exit=5   <source>:16:1: error: Instructions must be of an allowed type.
                           note: at 'unreachable' in block '#3' of function 'MainCS'.
hlsl_clang_trunk  exit=0
```

Confirmed locally on ground truth as well (`variant-clang-minimal-main-debug.txt`, exit
`0x80004005`), so the CE `dxc_trunk` result is not a CE artefact.

Same defect still reaches DXC; clang compiles it.  Reading clang's emitted DXIL, the default
label is the merge block and there is **no `unreachable`** -- the fall-off-the-end path
contributes `poison` to the phis:

```llvm
  switch i32 %2, label %5 [
    i32 2, label %4
    i32 1, label %3
  ], !dbg !121
...
5:                                                ; preds = %0, %3, %4
  %6 = phi nsz float [ 0.000000e+00, %4 ], [ 0.000000e+00, %3 ], [ poison, %0 ], !dbg !125
  ...
  call void @dx.op.bufferStore.f32(i32 69, %dx.types.Handle %10, i32 %1, i32 undef,
                                   float %6, float %7, float %8, float %9, i8 15)
  ret void
```

So on this construct clang already does what @llvm-beanz described.  Two limits on that
result, both real:

* it is one *restating*, not the issue's shader -- clang cannot compile the issue's shader
  (probe 3), so an exact comparison is not available;
* "no illegal instruction" is not the same as "correct": the undefined path now stores
  `poison`.  Whether that is the intended lowering is a clang question, not a DXC one.

> Trap worth recording: a naive `'unreachable' in output` check over the CE response says
> **True** for this shader.  The hit is in `!dx.source.contents` debug metadata, which embeds
> the HLSL source -- and the source is this file's own header comment, which contains the
> word.  The IR body has none.  Grep the function body, not the module.
